hero.title: Off the clock
hero.body: Not every thing I build has a brief behind it. This is the corner of the site for the ones that don't — starting with a keeper who reads your patterns.

game.title: Beat the keeper.
game.body: Pick a corner, then stop the timing bar in its sweet spot. The tighter the corner, the narrower that sweet spot — the better the shot has to be. And she watches where you shoot: keep going back to the same side and she will already be there.
steps: Pick a corner — click a zone, or press 1 to 9.
Stop the bar — Shoot, Space or Enter inside the green window.
Change sides — she learns the one you favour.
game.shootHint: Stop the bar in the green.
game.aimHint: Nine zones. She is expecting the easy one.
game.reducedMotion: Reduced motion is on, so the timing bar stays still and the strike is played for you. The keeper is exactly as hard.

save.read: She read it. Right where you aimed, and she was already there.
save.reach: Full stretch, fingertips — and it stays out.
save.weak: Scuffed it. Straight at her, and she smothers it.

goal.perfect: Struck perfectly. No keeper alive saves that one.
goal.wrongWay: She guessed the other side. You buried it.
goal.beaten: She got there — and it still went in. Goal.

wide.over: Over the bar. She did not have to move.
wide.post: Past the post. Close, and worth nothing.

score.rate: She is keeping out {pct} of everything on target, across {shots} shots this session.
score.empty: Nothing on the board yet. Take a shot.

note.body: Because the keeper is a system, not a coin flip: she keeps a record of where you shoot and spends it on her next guess. Building a thing that gets harder the more predictable you are turned out to be a better afternoon than any portfolio copy I could have written instead.
